reason: I'll make the cut first so the clotting response has a clear injury to address.
expectation: I expect the rough edge to break the skin and a small vessel, exposing a bleeding site.

alternatives.reason: Clotting factors may act on fibrinogen, but establishing the injury first seems more direct.

effect: The cut and narrowed vessel establish the bleeding site; platelets can now act there.
reaction: The narrowed vessel is a useful detail, though its role isn't explained yet.
reason: Platelets can help form an initial plug at the damaged vessel.
expectation: I expect platelets to gather at the cut and begin limiting bleeding, though a fibrin mesh may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: Making fibrin also supports clotting, but I want to address the cut with platelets first.

effect: The platelet plug slows the leak; the remaining offered combination may reinforce it.
reaction: The explanation clearly connects platelet gathering to reduced bleeding.
reason: This is the only available combination and should advance clotting.
expectation: I expect activated clotting factors to convert fibrinogen into fibrin, potentially forming a reinforcing mesh.

effect: Fibrin threads are available to reinforce the platelet plug.
reaction: The mesh among platelets makes its reinforcing role clear, though the conversion itself isn't explained.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should stabilize the plug.
expectation: I expect the fibrin mesh to strengthen the platelet plug and stop the bleeding.

effect: The fibrin mesh stabilized the platelet plug and stopped the bleeding, while the skin remains open.
reaction: The distinction between sealing the vessel and closing the skin is useful and satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reinforcing the platelet plug with fibrin was most worthwhile: the planned picture makes clear how the two components work together without implying the skin has healed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making fibrin threads was less informative than it could have been: the result shows the mesh but does not explain how the activated factors produce it from fibrinogen.

surprise.text: The vessel was already narrowed after the cut, but the picture did not explain what narrowing contributes.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the clotting-factor conversion was underexplained and the final two choices were the only offered combinations.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the still-open skin repairs after the bleeding stops, especially if the next chapter explains the mechanisms as clearly as the plug.
